idiom_name: Router(RoutingLogic, routees) / actor router pool with ConsistentHashingRoutingLogic
implementation_notes: An Akka router is a component that owns the destination set and the selection policy: router.route(msg, sender()) applies the RoutingLogic (consistent hashing for key-based routing, round-robin/random for balancing, broadcast and scatter-gather for fan-out) and routes from a pool of child routees or a group of existing actors. Watch routees and replace them on Terminated, and keep the logic immutable because Router and RoutingLogic are thread-safe and may be used outside actors. Choose it when the destinations are actors and the decision is a selection policy.
pitfalls: Unwatched routees vanish without a trace; Terminated handling is part of the router, not an optimisation.
Consistent hashing rebinds keys when the routee set changes, so per-key ordering guarantees must be re-examined after scaling.

variants.name: Akka Streams Partition graph stage
variants.implementation_notes: In a stream graph the routing decision is a stage: Partition fans the stream out to N outputs, each element is emitted to exactly the output its partitioner function returns, and backpressure is applied on the chosen output. The partitioner is a pure function of the element, which makes the rule set trivially testable and keeps the message untouched; the number of outputs is fixed when the graph is built, so this form suits stable topologies rather than frequently changing rule tables.
variants.code_sketch:
val p = b.add(Partition[Envelope](2, e => if (e.region == "eu") 0 else 1))
source ~> p.in
p.out(0) ~> euFlow
p.out(1) ~> usFlow
pitfalls: A partitioner index outside [0, N) fails the stream at runtime.
eagerCancel changes whether one cancelled downstream cancels the whole stage.
Merging the partitioned flows back loses the original order unless an ordered merge is used.
